html:
Amador, an enslaved man on São Tomé, led a revolt of plantation slaves in July 1595 that burned many of the island's sugar mills and plantations, and he proclaimed himself king.

His followers, said to number in the thousands, attacked the town of São Tomé itself. The Portuguese and their allies defeated them within weeks, and Amador was captured and executed in early 1596. The revolt and later raids by runaway communities in the forest helped end the sugar boom.

Today Rei Amador is the national hero of São Tomé and Príncipe. His face is on the banknotes, and 4 January is a public holiday in his name. He is one of the earliest named leaders of resistance to the slave trade.
